measured_at.note: All measurements below were taken by me at these SHAs. The committed prior report .scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/reports/24-audit.md was measured at frontend 7469d2789 / backend 45f8a2e99 and its counts have drifted; drift is quantified under PRD-C105.

criteria.evidence: NOT MET on every enforcement clause, verified at head. (a) TypeScript half absent: I read all four tsconfigs in full — streamlineos-backend/tsconfig.json, tsconfig.build.json, tsconfig.test.json and frontend/tsconfig.json — and none sets noUnusedLocals or noUnusedParameters; a repo-wide grep for those two flags across *.json/*.mjs/*.js/*.ts in BOTH repos (excluding node_modules/.next/.scratch) returns ZERO hits. (b) ESLint half configured but non-blocking: @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars is severity "warn" at streamlineos-backend/eslint.config.mjs:68-75 and frontend/eslint.config.mjs:20-23; `--max-warnings` appears NOWHERE in either repo (grep across *.yml/*.yaml/*.json/*.mjs = 0 hits) and CI runs a bare lint at streamlineos-backend/.github/workflows/ci.yml:53 (`pnpm lint`) and streamlineos-frontend/.github/workflows/frontend.yml:55 (`pnpm run lint`). A warn is therefore invisible to every gate. (c) Private members unchecked: `no-unused-private-class-members` is not configured in either eslint.config.mjs, and with noUnusedLocals off nothing covers the TypeScript `private` modifier at all. (d) The `_` escape the criterion forbids is configured three ways in BOTH repos — argsIgnorePattern AND varsIgnorePattern AND caughtErrorsIgnorePattern all `^_` — where the criterion permits only a named `_` PARAMETER at a framework/interface callback position. It is in live use on non-framework positions: `_userId` on the module's own service methods at src/modules/support/core/support-drafts.service.ts:20,33,47; support-macros.service.ts:49,70; support-workspace.service.ts:79,97,113,132; src/modules/build/comment-drafts/comment-drafts.service.ts:26,137,170,188; src/modules/notifications/notification-preference-rules.service.ts:33,41; and `_eventKey` on an exported plain function at src/modules/notifications/notification-delivery-class.ts:115. MEASURED SURFACE at head, by my own eslint runs (`nice -n 15 npx eslint "src/**/*.ts" -f json` backend; `nice -n 15 npx eslint -f json` frontend): backend 5,817 files linted, 273 errors / 387 warnings, 368 no-unused-vars findings (189 in non-spec files); frontend 5,492 files linted, 4 errors / 906 warnings, 751 no-unused-vars findings (724 in non-test files). 1,119 unused-symbol findings at head and not one fails a gate. Hand-verified one: src/common/auth/principal.ts:130 declares `function principalAuditIdentity(principal: Principal): PrincipalAuditIdentity` and `grep -rn principalAuditIdentity src/ test/` returns exactly ONE line — the declaration itself. Corroborating and decisive: streamlineos-frontend/CLAUDE.md section 6 records this as a DELIBERATE non-adoption — 'Unused-symbol enforcement is NOT on, and the underscore escape is why... Deliberately left off for the 10/10 code release... Tracked as a NEW REQUIREMENT needing an owner. Do not turn it on without owning the migration and deleting the three ^_ patterns in the same change.' It also records the full-strength measurement: 4,186 violations across 1,896 files, 2,912 of them (69.6%) naming a `_`-prefixed identifier. PRD checkbox at architecture-refactor/PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md:197 is still '- [ ]'.
criteria.blocker: No enforcement mechanism exists in either repo: the TypeScript flags are absent, the ESLint rule cannot fail a job (warn + no --max-warnings anywhere), private members have no rule, and the three ^_ ignore patterns actively license the rename the criterion forbids. To close: set noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters or move no-unused-vars to "error" with --max-warnings 0 in both lint scripts and both CI workflows, add no-unused-private-class-members, DELETE the three ^_ patterns in the same change (CLAUDE.md section 6 makes this explicit), and clear the ~1,119 findings — removing the symbols, not renaming them. Note the documented trap: --noUnusedParameters exempts _-prefixed parameters by construction and cannot see a catch binding, so tsc alone cannot enforce this criterion.
criteria.clauses_failing: ALL FOUR enforcement clauses fail: (1) 'Enable and enforce TypeScript ... unused-symbol checks' — flags absent from all 4 tsconfigs; (2) 'enforce ... ESLint unused-symbol checks' — configured at warn, no --max-warnings in either repo, CI runs bare lint, so 1,119 live findings pass every gate; (3) '... and private members' — no rule of any kind covers them; (4) 'Remove unused symbols instead of renaming them to _ ... allow a named _ parameter only where a framework/interface callback contract requires its position' — varsIgnorePattern and caughtErrorsIgnorePattern are escapes the criterion never permits, argsIgnorePattern is blanket rather than framework-scoped, and 18 verified _userId/_eventKey sites sit on the modules' own service methods and an exported plain function.

criteria.evidence: An inventory DOES exist and IS committed — .scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/reports/24-audit.md section 1, tracked in git (`git ls-files` matches it; last touched by commit a6521b59d 'docs+fix(release): 36 ticket audits, the closure definition, and the frontend repairs') — and it does carry a count for each of the 16 dimensions the criterion names. (3) NO RE-DERIVABLE ARTIFACT AND NO GATE. The report's own section 5 lists 'A committed inventory artifact' under 'Not measured / blocked'. The PRD checkbox at architecture-refactor/PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md:346 is still '- [ ]' and the traceability manifest row (.scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/TRACEABILITY.md:118) is unchanged, which the ticket's Completion evidence section requires be flipped in the same commit.
criteria.blocker: The inventory is a one-shot markdown count table taken at a superseded SHA, with no generator and no gate, so it cannot be re-derived or kept true; it has already drifted by 8 migrations, 58 specs and 99 backend source files. To close: emit the inventory from a script (one row per module folder / controller / DTO-schema / schema file / migration / worker / cache key / event consumer / frontend route / component / hook / TanStack key / test / fixture / operational script), wire it to a check:* gate with an anti-vacuity floor so it cannot pass over an empty walk, commit the generated artifact, and flip PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md:346 plus the TRACEABILITY row in that same commit.
criteria.clauses_failing: The single 'Inventory its ...' clause fails on completeness and currency, not on coverage of the 16 named dimensions: all 16 are counted, but none is enumerated, the counts are stale at head by measured amounts (+8 migrations, +58 specs, +99 src .ts, +103 kebab-scan entries, -8 cross-feature baseline), and no regenerating gate exists.

criteria.evidence: Four-clause criterion; ONE clause substantively holds, THREE fail. (i) KEBAB-CASE NAMING — HOLDS, over a real corpus. Backend `check:kebab-case` exits 0: '/tmp/beg-check_kebab-case.log: scanned 6646 entries under src — 0 violation(s), 2 of 2 recorded exceptions still present' against 6,057 files under src/ (the surplus is directories), so this is a genuine population, not a vacuous pass. The frontend has NO kebab gate at all (grep for 'kebab' across frontend/scripts/ and package.json = 0 hits), so I measured it myself: 0 non-kebab .ts/.tsx filenames under app,components,features,hooks,lib, and the only non-kebab directories are the __tests__ convention plus components/hr/_onboarding. Naming holds; its frontend enforcement does not exist. (ii) CORRECT IMPORT DIRECTION — FAILS, three ways. (ii-a) The backend detector is near-vacuous: '/tmp/beg-check_import-direction.log: scanned 233 files under src/common — 0 new violation(s), 0 of 0 baseline entries still present'. 233 of the 5,817 .ts files under src/ is 4.0% of the tree, and by its own header (src/scripts/check-import-direction.mjs:6) it checks exactly ONE direction, src/common -> src/modules. Cross-module deep imports — src/modules/a reaching into src/modules/b's internals, the direction this criterion is actually about — are checked by nothing in the backend. (ii-b) `check:cycles` is RED (exit 1). /tmp/beg-check_cycles.log: 'Processed 5825 files ... Found 1 circular dependency! 1) modules/notifications/notification-delivery-worker.service.ts > modules/notifications/notification-delivery-preflight.ts'. I verified it by hand at head: src/modules/notifications/notification-delivery-worker.service.ts:51 `import { resolveDeliveryPreflight } from "./notification-delivery-preflight"` and src/modules/notifications/notification-delivery-preflight.ts:9 `import type { QueueRunResult } from "./notification-delivery-worker.service"`. A cycle is by definition not a correct import direction, and streamlineos-frontend/CLAUDE.md section 9 asserts 'both repos are at zero' — that statement is false at head. (ii-c) The frontend gate exits 0 only because violations are BASELINED: /tmp/feg-check_import-direction.log reads 'shared-imports-feature: 3/3 (at baseline)' and 'cross-feature-import: 169/169 (at baseline)' against BASELINE_SHARED_IMPORTS_FEATURE = 3 (frontend/scripts/check-import-direction.mjs:42) and BASELINE_CROSS_FEATURE = 169 (:62). 172 live wrong-direction imports are permanently accepted by a green gate. (iii) ONE CANONICAL DOMAIN OWNER — FAILS, and NO detector exists. I searched src/scripts/*.mjs and frontend/scripts/*.mjs for any canonical-ownership or parallel-location check: none exists in either repo. Measured at head by mapping every non-spec @Controller prefix to its owning src/modules/<folder>: 14 top-level route prefixes are served by MORE THAN ONE module folder — public (9 owners: ai build e-sign feedbucket hr kb public storage surveys), crm (6: activities autonomy crm data-quality ingress issues), hr (5: email expenses hr payroll storage), webhooks (4: billing calendar email webhooks), settings (3: automation email settings), me (3: api-tokens expenses hr), and 8 more with 2 owners each including accounting and finance. (iv) NO PARALLEL LEGACY/DUPLICATE LOCATION — FAILS. Backend: src/modules/finance holds 234 .ts and src/modules/accounting 91 .ts, and they interleave — 36 non-spec controllers UNDER finance/ carry @Controller("accounting...") while src/modules/accounting/ai/accounting-ai.controller.ts:23 carries @Controller("finance/ai"); the schema layer already consolidated on accounting yet 7 files under src/db/schema/accounting/ are still named finance-*.ts (finance-ar-ap, finance-assets, finance-banking, finance-expenses, finance-planning, finance-report-export-jobs, finance-tax). Frontend: 12 domain names exist as BOTH components/<x> and features/<x> — hr (19 vs 580 files), inventory (5 vs 118), blog (10 vs 9), dashboard (7 vs 34), support (2 vs 71), settings (1 vs 85), organization (5 vs 1), billing (1 vs 33), auth (2 vs 6), feedbucket (1 vs 3), shared (22 vs 13), plus __tests__.
criteria.blocker: Two of the four clauses have NO detector at all (canonical domain owner, parallel/duplicate location) and the third has a detector that reads 4% of the backend tree in one direction while the frontend's exits green over 172 baselined violations. Nothing in either repo would notice a new split-ownership prefix or a new components/<x> duplicate of features/<x>. To close: (1) add an ownership gate that maps every controller route prefix and every schema table to exactly one module folder and fails on a second owner, seeded with the 14 measured splits as a strictly-decreasing ratchet; (2) extend backend check:import-direction beyond src/common to the full src/modules cross-module direction, or state its 4% reach in its own output so it cannot be read as tree-wide; (3) fix the notifications cycle so check:cycles returns to 0; (4) drive BASELINE_CROSS_FEATURE 169 -> 0 rather than holding it; (5) add a frontend kebab-case gate so that clause is enforced and not merely true today.
criteria.clauses_failing: Clause 1 'kebab-case naming' HOLDS on the backend over 6,646 scanned entries and holds by my own measurement on the frontend, though the frontend has no gate. Clause 2 'correct import direction' FAILS — backend detector reads 233 of 5,817 src files (4.0%) in one direction only, check:cycles is exit 1 on a verified notifications cycle, and the frontend gate is green over 169 + 3 baselined violations. Clause 3 'one canonical domain owner' FAILS — no detector in either repo, and 14 backend route prefixes have 2-9 owning module folders. Clause 4 'no parallel legacy/duplicate location' FAILS — accounting/finance is a 325-file two-folder duplication with 36 cross-serving controllers and 7 residual finance-*.ts schema files, and 12 frontend domains have both a components/ and a features/ home.

criteria.evidence: No per-file KEEP/REFACTOR/REMOVE classification exists in either repo. What exists is two things, and I measured the reach of both. (1) A PROSE CLASSIFICATION, committed at .scratch/code-release-10-10-v2/reports/24-audit.md section PRD-C107 (commit a6521b59d): 9 REFACTOR groups covering ~320 files and 6 REMOVE groups, each naming the failure it prevents, with KEEP-by-default asserted for the remaining ~11,000 files. That report's own summary states it 'is not the per-file artifact the criterion and the ticket's completion-evidence section ask for'. (2) A MACHINE-READABLE LEDGER inside src/scripts/check-dead-code.mjs carrying FIVE verdicts — 1 KEEP, 2 WIRE, 2 REMOVE — plus 2 RETAINED-BY-CONTRACT, against a corpus of roughly 11,000 files. CORPUS CHECK ON THE DETECTORS THAT UNDERPIN THE KEEP-BY-DEFAULT HALF — both are genuinely non-vacuous and I credit them: frontend /tmp/feg-check_dead-code.log reports its own reach explicitly, 'check-dead-code (knip findings): scanned 104 of 104 findings (100%) — the whole corpus' and 'check-dead-code (module graph): scanned 5408 of 5408 files (100%) — the whole corpus', Baseline files=0 exports=0, Current files=0 exports=0, UNCLASSIFIED (0); backend /tmp/beg-check_dead-code.log reports 'knip: 0 unused file(s), 7 other finding(s) | importer graph: 9932 files, 69914 edges' with all 7 findings classified. Those are real populations. BUT ONE OF THE SEVEN BACKEND VERDICTS IS JUSTIFIED BY A NON-PRODUCT FILE. The RETAINED-BY-CONTRACT entry reads: '[type] src/modules/ai/core/dto/request.schemas.ts:MeetingPrepInput — inferred type of meetingPrepSchema, which is parsed at a live boundary in .claude/worktrees/bold-napier-7a4a41/src/modules/ai/core/controllers/crm-ai.controller.ts'. I checked both trees: the worktree copy does reference it (:41 and :188, `@Body(new ZodValidationPipe(meetingPrepSchema))`), but the MAIN-tree controller of the identical path, src/modules/ai/core/controllers/crm-ai.controller.ts, exists and does NOT — `grep -rn meetingPrepSchema src/` returns exactly two lines, its own declaration and type alias at src/modules/ai/core/dto/request.schemas.ts:64,71. src/scripts/check-dead-code.mjs does not prune .claude/worktrees (2 worktrees present at head). In a clean CI checkout that symbol is unreferenced, so its retention verdict is unfounded — a classification held up by a transient agent worktree. THE REMOVE VERDICTS ARE UN-ACTIONED AT HEAD. `validateConfig` still has 1 interface declaration (src/modules/notifications/providers/notification-provider.interface.ts:11) plus 5 implementations (sandbox, web-push, sms, email, whatsapp providers) and ZERO callers — 6 grep hits in src/, all declarations. The five committed session-forgery scripts are still tracked AT HEAD (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` lists frontend/.scratch/admission-probe.mjs, admission-probe2.mjs, mint-session.mjs, probe-exchange.mjs, probe-exchange2.mjs) despite .gitignore:8 listing frontend/.scratch/; mint-session.mjs opens by deriving the NextAuth session key with hkdf and minting an EncryptJWT session token. CORROBORATING REGRESSION: `check:over-300` is RED (exit 1) — /tmp/beg-check_over-300.log: '402 files exceed 300 lines — 10 above baseline of 392', topped by src/modules/organization/core/membership-artifacts.ts at 3,216 lines. Ten files crossed the threshold with no REFACTOR verdict attached to any of them. PRD checkbox at architecture-refactor/PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md:348 is still '- [ ]'.
criteria.blocker: The criterion asks for a verdict on EVERY inventoried file; head has 5 symbol-level verdicts in a gate script plus a prose grouping of ~320 files in a report, against roughly 11,000 files, and no per-file artifact or gate exists. Two further blockers must be cleared in the same pass: (a) check-dead-code.mjs must prune .claude/worktrees so a verdict cannot be justified by a file absent from a clean checkout — re-run it there and MeetingPrepInput will need a real verdict; (b) PRD-C105 is OPEN, so there is no enumerated inventory to classify against. To close: emit one row per inventoried file with KEEP/REFACTOR/REMOVE and, for every non-KEEP row, the concrete failure prevented; gate it so an unclassified file fails; then flip PRD-10-10-CODE-RELEASE-TODO.md:348 and the TRACEABILITY row in the same commit.
criteria.clauses_failing: Clause 1 'Classify every inventoried file as KEEP, REFACTOR or REMOVE' FAILS — 5 machine-readable verdicts + ~320 prose-grouped files against ~11,000; KEEP-by-default is a policy, not a per-file classification; and one of the 7 backend verdicts (MeetingPrepInput, RETAINED-BY-CONTRACT) rests on a .claude/worktrees path that does not exist in a clean checkout. Clause 2 'name the concrete failure prevented for each REFACTOR/REMOVE verdict' HOLDS for the verdicts that do exist — every REFACTOR group in the report and every REMOVE/WIRE entry in check-dead-code.mjs carries a written failure — but is untestable at scale because clause 1 has not produced the population.
